comparisons.peer_summary: Unrecognized tax benefits impacting the effective tax rate were $1.3 billion as of 2024 and 2023, with accrued penalties and interest of $298 million; long-term income tax liabilities for these benefits totaled $1.4 billion as of 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose long-term income tax liabilities specifically attributed to the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act transition tax and/or uncertain tax positions. Intel reports $1.6 billion in long-term income taxes payable primarily composed of the transition tax payable over eight years. AMD reports $1.4 billion in long-term income tax liabilities related to unrecognized tax benefits, noting that $1.3 billion of these benefits would impact the effective tax rate if recognized. While Intel explicitly itemizes the transition tax as a major driver of its long-term payable, AMD groups long-term liabilities under unrecognized tax benefits without explicitly breaking out the transition tax component in the cited text, though both address significant long-term tax obligations.

sentences.text: Long-term income taxes payable of $1.6 billion as of December 28, 2024 ($2.6 billion as of December 30, 2023) are primarily composed of the transition tax from Tax Reform, which is payable over eight years beginning in 2018, as well as amounts for uncertain tax positions, reduced by the associated deduction for state taxes and non-US tax credits.

As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the Company had long-term income tax liabilities related to unrecognized tax benefits of $1.4 billion, recorded under Other long-term liabilities in the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheets.

The amount of unrecognized tax benefits that would impact the effective tax rate if recognized was $1.3 billion, $1.3 billion and $1.2 billion as of December 28, 2024, December 30, 2023 and December 31, 2022, respectively.

comparisons.peer_topic: Unrecognized Tax Benefits Reconciliation and Amounts
comparisons.peer_summary: The company recognized $144 million, $22 million, and $25 million in interest and penalties during fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively, with total accrued interest and penalties reaching approximately $701 million as of November 3, 2024, primarily due to the VMware acquisition and current year accruals. Approximately $6,544 million and $5,044 million of unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest and penalties would benefit the effective income tax rate if recognized as of November 3, 2024, and October 29, 2023, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Broadcom both disclose the nature and amount of unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest/penalties as part of their long-term tax positions. Intel cites amounts for uncertain tax positions as part of its $1.6 billion long-term payable. Broadcom provides specific reconciliation details, stating that approximately $6,544 million of unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest/penalties would benefit the effective income tax rate if recognized. Broadcom also discloses significant accrued interest and penalties ($701 million), whereas Intel does not specify the interest/penalty component within the cited long-term payable figure, focusing instead on the transition tax and uncertain positions generally.

sentences.text: Long-term income taxes payable of $1.6 billion as of December 28, 2024 ($2.6 billion as of December 30, 2023) are primarily composed of the transition tax from Tax Reform, which is payable over eight years beginning in 2018, as well as amounts for uncertain tax positions, reduced by the associated deduction for state taxes and non-US tax credits.

As of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, approximately $6,544 million and $5,044 million, respectively, of the unrecognized tax benefits and accrued interest and penalties would, if recognized, benefit our effective income tax rate.
The increase in total accrued interest and penalties was primarily the result of the VMware acquisition in addition to the current year accrual.

comparisons.peer_topic: NOL and tax credit carryforwards and unrecognized tax benefits
comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, gross unrecognized tax benefits were $716 million (potentially impacting the effective tax rate by ~$633 million); while interest and penalties were not significant, the estimated reduction in unrecognized benefits in the next 12 months is not expected to be significant despite uncertain resolution timing.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron both disclose gross unrecognized tax benefits that could impact the effective tax rate. Intel includes amounts for uncertain tax positions within its long-term income taxes payable. Micron explicitly quantifies its gross unrecognized tax benefits at $716 million, which would have an impact of approximately $633 million on its effective tax rate if recognized. Unlike Intel, which groups uncertain tax positions into a broader long-term payable figure alongside the transition tax, Micron isolates the unrecognized benefit amount and its specific rate impact, while also noting that accrued interest and penalties were not significant.

As of August 29, 2024, gross unrecognized tax benefits were $716 million, which would have an impact of approximately $633 million on our effective tax rate in the future, if recognized.

comparisons.peer_summary: Income tax payable is comprised of the long-term portion of the one-time transition tax payable, unrecognized tax benefits, and related interest and penalties.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both identify the one-time transition tax and unrecognized tax benefits as key components of their long-term income tax payables. Intel reports $1.6 billion in long-term income taxes payable, primarily consisting of the transition tax payable over eight years and amounts for uncertain tax positions. NVIDIA similarly states that its income tax payable is comprised of the long-term portion of the one-time transition tax payable, unrecognized tax benefits, and related interest and penalties. Both companies explicitly link their long-term tax liabilities to the legacy transition tax obligation from the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.
